issue.title: [Bug] Writing metadata to a CBZ fails with `FILE_ENDED` when the archive has a ZIP comment
issue.body:
### What went wrong?

Saving metadata to a `.cbz` fails with a`FILE_ENDED` error whenever the archive has a non-empty ZIP comment.
The archive itself is valid (`unzip -t` passes, the reader opens it) but writing from bookorbit fails.

ComicTagger seems to store some `ComicBookInfo` JSON blob in the ZIP archive comment, so every comic tagged with ComicTagger's ComicBookInfo option probably will have this issue.

The problem is probably with the `unzipper` library, that only reads the last 80 bytes of a file by default to search for the end-of-directory signature.

With a long comment, the end of file record becomes longer than 80 bytes, so the signature is not found.
The ZIP spec allows comments up to 65535 bytes, so the 80 bytes could be much longer.

`unzipper` has the option to pass an `options.tailSize` to allow more bytes to be searched, so either expanding this by default or trying with a bigger value if an `FILE_ENDED` error occurs might be a potential fix.

Removing the  comment from such a files fixes the issue.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take any valid CBZ and add a ZIP comment longer than  about 58 bytes (I have attached a test file, change the file extension to cbz to use: [comment-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31836933/comment-repro.zip)
2. In BookOrbit, enable "write changes back to files" for the library.
3. Edit any writable field (title, series, tags, …) on that book and save.



### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: `ComicInfo.xml` inside the archive is updated.
Actual: the write fails with error: `FILE_ENDED`.

### Your setup

- BookOrbit: v2.4.0 (also present on `main`)
- Deployment: Docker
- OS: Truenas
- Browser: Firefox 155

### Relevant logs (optional)

```shell
{"level":40,"time":1788526138690,"pid":8,"hostname":"bef483c9b55b","req":{"id":"req-1je","method":"POST","url":"/api/v1/books/2217/write-and-rename"},"context":"FileWriteService","msg":"[file_write.write] [fail] bookId=2217 format=cbz triggeredBy=sync userId=1 dryRun=false durationMs=31 errorClass=Error error=\"FILE_ENDED\" - file write failed"}
{"level":30,"time":1788526138721,"pid":8,"hostname":"bef483c9b55b","req":{"id":"req-1je","method":"POST","url":"/api/v1/books/2217/write-and-rename"},"context":"FileWriteService","msg":"[file_write.write] [end] bookId=2217 format=cbz triggeredBy=sync userId=1 dryRun=false durationMs=61 status=failed fieldsWritten=0 reason=\"FILE_ENDED\" - file write completed"}
```

issue.title: [Bug] BookOrbit incorrectly detects Goodreads responses as challenge pages
issue.body:
### What went wrong?

Some background information first: I was really annoyed by the Goodreads anti-bot challenges and the fact that a lot of my metadata searches hit that issue so by using a DNS and private certificate hack I am forcing BookOrbit to talk to another service of mine that pre-caches Goodreads pages and returns the HTML to BookOrbit so I don’t hit that issue.

I realised though that even the cached legitimate pages trigger a challenge detection (incorrectly as the full page with metadata is actually present). I have resolved that on my side by just removing the offending part from the cached HTML before returning it to BookOrbit but thought I should probably raise a bug as well to get it fixed at the source.

The offending part in the HTML looks like `<script src="...challenge.js"...>` but that exists even in valid response pages

### Steps to reproduce

  1. Enable Goodreads as a metadata provider in BookOrbit.
  2. Start a metadata lookup for any Goodreads book while Goodreads returns a normal book HTML page.
  3. Ensure the returned HTML contains valid book markers such as data-testid="bookTitle" and Goodreads og:site_name, plus Goodreads’ WAF script reference:
     <script src="...challenge.js"...>
      This step will probably require a temporary change in BookOrbit to save the returned Goodreads response in a file or log it somewhere
  4. BookOrbit’s Goodreads provider receives the response and runs isWafChallenge(status, html).
  5. The challenge.js match causes the valid book response to be classified as a bot challenge before the book HTML is parsed.

I provided an example HTML as well. That is a valid goodreads response that contains all the metadata but it also contains:
```
<script src="https://b13c77965523.us-east-1.sdk.awswaf.com/b13c77965523/d42dcdc33310/challenge.js" data-nscript="afterInteractive"></script>
```
which triggers the false positive

[example.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31703080/example.html)

### Expected vs actual behavior

Valid responses should be processed but they are rejected

### Your setup

- BookOrbit version: latest (2.8.1)
- Deployment: Docker
- OS: Debian 13
- Browser: Safari

issue.title: [Bug] Numeric-prefixed Hardcover slug is parsed as a book ID, linking the wrong book
issue.body:
### What went wrong?

When `book_metadata.hardcover_id` holds a Hardcover slug that begins with digits, the `metadata_id` match step treats the leading number as a Hardcover book ID instead of resolving the slug.

"84, Charing Cross Road" has the slug `84-charing-cross-road`, so it links to Hardcover book **84**, which is *The Ultimate Sales Machine*. Reading progress then syncs to that book.

This looks like a `parseInt` on the saved provider ID, since `parseInt("84-charing-cross-road", 10) === 84`. Slugs without a numeric prefix are unaffected because they parse to `NaN` and fall through to a real slug lookup (`the-shadow-of-the-wind` resolves correctly to 375470).

Suggested fix: only treat the provider ID as numeric when the entire string is numeric, e.g. `/^\d+$/.test(providerId)` rather than `parseInt`, and resolve by slug otherwise.

Workaround: clear the cached match and null out `hardcover_id` so ISBN matching takes over. Re-saving the book from Search online reintroduces the bad slug.

Related but distinct: #411 covers the stored work slug bypassing ISBN search and returning the wrong *edition*. This one lands on an entirely different *book*, and only for slugs that start with a digit.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a book whose Hardcover slug starts with a number, e.g. `84-charing-cross-road`, saved in metadata as the Hardcover provider ID.
2. Make sure there is no cached match, so the `metadata_id` step actually runs: `delete from hardcover_book_state where book_id = <id>;`
3. Trigger a Hardcover sync.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: the book links to Hardcover book 277100, "84, Charing Cross Road".

Actual: it links to Hardcover book 84, "The Ultimate Sales Machine". The book shows as "Linked (Metadata match)" and the edition picker lists only editions of that book.

```
 book_id | hardcover_book_id | match_method
---------+-------------------+--------------
      31 |                84 | metadata_id
```

Control, to rule out bad ISBN or title metadata. Same book, same empty cache, the only change being `hardcover_id` set to null so matching falls through to ISBN-13 (`9780140143508`):

```
 book_id | hardcover_book_id | hardcover_edition_id | match_method
---------+-------------------+----------------------+--------------
      31 |            277100 |             15528636 | isbn
```

That isolates the numeric-prefixed slug as the cause.

### Your setup

BookOrbit 2.8.1, self-hosted in Kubernetes (k3s) from `ghcr.io/bookorbit/bookorbit:2.8.1`, Postgres 16, Linux host. Hardcover sync enabled, progress arriving over KOSync from a third-party reader.

### Relevant logs (optional)

```shell
Wrong match, made fresh with an empty cache and the correct slug in metadata:


[hardcover.sync_book] [end] userId=1 bookId=31 hardcoverBookId=84 hardcoverEditionId=22486732
  hardcoverUserBookId=18071070 hardcoverReadId=6573652 matchMethod=metadata_id statusId=2 - synced


Resulting row:


 book_id | hardcover_book_id | hardcover_edition_id | match_method |          created_at
---------+-------------------+----------------------+--------------+-------------------------------
      31 |                84 |             22486732 | metadata_id  | 2026-09-01 23:29:50.80126+00


Metadata that produced it:


 book_id |         title          |    isbn13     |     hardcover_id
---------+------------------------+---------------+-----------------------
      31 | 84, Charing Cross Road | 9780140143508 | 84-charing-cross-road
```

issue.title: [Bug] Potential compatibility issue in BookOrbit PR build when testing Prowlarr indexer: upstream responds 406 and app surfaces 502
issue.body:
I’m aware this is a PR build rather than a released version, but I still think this is worth reporting because it looks like a compatibility issue between the BookOrbit PR build and the Prowlarr API behavior in this version pair.

I’m opening this as an awareness / bug report while testing a BookOrbit PR build. I’m aware this is not a tagged release and not a production-ready build, but I wanted to test the feature and I believe this may still be a real compatibility issue worth reporting.


### What went wrong?

When testing the Prowlarr integration from within BookOrbit, the request to validate an indexer fails upstream with a 406 response from Prowlarr. BookOrbit then surfaces a 502 and logs a generic ASP.NET formatter warning instead of a clear integration error.

I’m not treating this as a stable release issue, because I’m intentionally using a PR build, but I think this is still worth reporting because the current behavior appears to be a compatibility problem between the BookOrbit PR build and the Prowlarr version in use, and the error handling is not clear enough to diagnose it quickly.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Run BookOrbit PR build:
   - `ghcr.io/bookorbit/bookorbit:pr-1116-30ed4f65185f`
2. Run Prowlarr:
   - `ghcr.io/hotio/prowlarr:release-2.3.0.5236`
3. In BookOrbit, open the book request / indexer configuration screen.
4. Add or select a Prowlarr-backed indexer using the Torznab integration.
5. Trigger the “test” action for that indexer.
6. Observe the request:
   - `POST /api/v1/admin/request-indexers/1/test`
7. Result:
   - BookOrbit logs:
     ```json
     {"context":"TorznabAdapter","msg":"[request_indexer.test] [fail] indexerId=1 error=\"Prowlarr answered 406\" - torznab test failed"}
     ```
   - then:
     ```json
     {"context":"GlobalExceptionFilter","err":{"type":"BadGatewayException","message":"Prowlarr answered 406", ...},"status":502}
     ```
   - and the HTTP response is `502`.
8. In the app logs, you also see:
   ```text
   [Warn] Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Infrastructure.ObjectResultExecutor: No output formatter was found for content types 'application/json' to write the response.
   ```
9. The issue is reproducing consistently when the indexer test hits the Prowlarr endpoint.


### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected behavior:
The test should either succeed or fail with a clear and actionable integration error.

Actual behavior:
The request fails upstream with `Prowlarr answered 406`, BookOrbit turns it into HTTP 502, and the app logs a generic JSON formatter warning that hides the actual upstream cause.

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- Ingress: NGINX Ingress

issue.title: [Bug] PDF Cover generator ignoring crop box
issue.body: ### What went wrong? When importing a PDF whose cover page defines a CropBox smaller than its MediaBox (a common technique for embedding a full wraparound cover — back cover + spine + front cover — on a single page while only the front cover is meant to be visible), BookOrbit's thumbnail generator renders the full MediaBox instead of respecting the CropBox. The result is that the library thumbnail and cover art show the entire wraparound spread — back cover, spine text, and barcode included — rather than just the front cover. ### Steps to reproduce I1. mport a PDF where the cover page has a MediaBox larger than its CropBox (e.g. a Steve Jackson Games / GURPS PDF — many of their titles are built this way, with the visible page being a CropBox crop of a larger MediaBox that contains the full wraparound cover art). 2. Let BookOrbit scan the file and generate its cover thumbnail. 3. View the book's thumbnail in the library grid or detail page. ### Expected vs actual behavior **Expected Behavior** The thumbnail should reflect only the CropBox region of the cover page — i.e. the front cover as any standard PDF viewer (Preview, Adobe Reader, Skim, etc.) would display it. **Actual Behavior** The thumbnail shows the entire MediaBox region: the full wraparound spread (back cover, spine, and front cover all in one image), effectively squeezing the front cover into a fraction of the thumbnail and surrounding it with content that was never meant to be visible. ### Your setup - BookOrbit Version: docker latest - currently 2.70 - Deployment method: docker compose - Server OS: Fedora Linux 44 - Client Browser: Firefox 154.0.1 ### Relevant logs (optional) ```shell ``` ### Screenshots (optional) ### Before submitting - [x] I've searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet. - [x] If I implement this fix, I will wait for maintainer approval and assignment before writing code or opening a pull request.

Add an option to the advanced fetch behaviour for the in field rules. It should set the autofill feature in the book metadata to only use configured provider IDs and not try to use any others.

### What problem does it solve?

If the provider ID has been confirmed by checking, and the autofill button is pressed, then other results wont accidentally get added into the book metadata. Only updates from the existing sources will be added - for example ratings.

### Anything else? (optional)

issue.body: ### What's your idea? When in the web reader, show where the current page is, for example by highlighting the current chapter/section/et. in the tree. ### What problem does it solve? When navigating via contents, it would make it easier to see where the reader is currently positioned. ### Anything else? (optional) Given that navigation via contents works flawlessly, I would assume it should be fairly easy for the reader to figure out where its current page fits into the book's chapters. ### Want to help?
